answer: Interleaved Half-Sonnet Joining: new identities may only submit their first transactions at randomly scheduled slots, spaced at least one full sonnet cycle apart across independent channels. Each acceptance requires a small unique anchor token tied to that slot, preventing bulk parallel registration. A pearl of verified history accumulates only through correctly timed repeats. An attacker cloning N identities pays N distinct timing costs and loses throughput to forced spacing, making mass sybil creation slower and costlier than honest growth.
